title: Secret generation manifest
description:
What one immutable generation under /var/lib/agentic-postgres/secrets/<key>/generations/<id>/ contains: which declared secrets were materialized, to which consumer, at which path, owned by whom.

It describes placement and never content. No secret value appears here, and no digest of one either -- a digest would make the manifest a verification oracle for a value it must not reveal, and §16 already refuses digests as an isolation substitute. Proof that a consumer got its own secret is the mount list plus a successful read by that consumer, not a hash anyone can compare.

generation_id.description: Random and unordered, not a timestamp: ordered names invite an operator to reason about which generation is newest when what matters is which one is active.

name.description: The declared name from secrets.required.yaml. Not the provider key: where a value came from is bootstrap state's business, and repeating it here would put the provider layout into a file mounted next to the values.

items.description: A `compose` consumer names the service that mounts the file; a `root` consumer names none, because no container holds the value (ADR 0054). `service` is required for the first and absent for the second, so a manifest cannot record a root-plane file as though a service had it.

target_file.description: The file's basename inside the generation. **The same pattern as secret-contract.schema.json's `target_file`, and a test asserts the two are identical** (D586). This one was stricter -- letter-first where the contract allows letter-or-digit -- and the difference was invisible until a target file began with a digit.

uid.description: The consumer's fixed numeric UID (D21). Compose's uid/gid/mode fields are not relied on, so the host owns the file before anything mounts it.

mode.description: Octal, as written in the secret contract. Owner-read-only in practice.

format.description: What the materializer wrote into this file. **The same set as secret-contract.schema.json's `format`, and a test asserts the two are identical** (D586): they are two schemas over one concept, and they disagreed for a whole session -- `pgbackrest` was added to the contract in Run 8b and not here, so every Session 10 deploy failed at materialization with a schema error naming a format the contract had just declared legal.
